transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Sonia Wu (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood CSM); Marcus Lee (CTO, EdgeWorks), Anita Gomez (Head of MLOps), Tomás Rivera (Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
EdgeWorks is evaluating dedicated reserved GPU pools with hybrid fallback to hosted. Key concerns: isolation for multi-tenant data, burst handling for sudden user spikes (~10x baseline), pre-warm latency SLOs, and on-prem connectivity for a subset of workloads. They requested pricing scenarios and a technical deep dive around NVLink/locality and VPC egress.

Topics: dedicated sizing, isolation models, burst policy, VPC/private connectivity, compliance artifacts, pilot success criteria

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Marcus, Anita, Tomás — do you want to do quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus (EdgeWorks): Yeah, Marcus Lee here, CTO. We're building a customer-facing generative assistant for field service. Need low p95 latency and cost predictability.
[00:22] Anita: Anita, Head of MLOps. I own model infra and runbooks. We'll be the primary implementers.
[00:27] Tomás: Tomás — infra lead, networking and on-prem stuff.
[00:31] Jamie: Great. Quick agenda — understand current stack and traffic patterns, talk dedicated reserved pools and isolation options, burst strategy, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:40] Marcus: Yep.

[01:05] Sonia (Redwood SE): Quick note — I'll be the tech lead on our side. I'll ask about sequence lengths, KV cache usage, and any strict data residency. Those details change recommended instance mixes.
[01:18] Anita: Sequence lengths are 512 tokens avg, spikes to 2k for long context in some case types. We use a small KV cache for session resume.

[02:05] Jamie: Good — that tells us we need to size for occasional long context. What's your baseline QPS and burst multiple?
[02:12] Marcus: Baseline is about 12 rps across our fleet; during campaign spikes we see up to 120 rps for ~10–15 minutes — so roughly 10x. We're expecting growth to steady 40 rps in next six months.
[02:30] Sonia: Are those user-perceived latencies? What's your P95 target?
[02:34] Marcus: P95 under 450 ms is ideal, but we can tolerate up to 700ms during spikes.

[03:10] Tomás: Network wise we have peered VPCs for most traffic. Some customers require on-prem processing behind firewall, so we may need a hybrid pattern where sensitive documents go to our on-prem cluster, and non-sensitive go to cloud.
[03:28] Priya: On compliance — SOC2 in progress, some contracts need encrypted keys in customer KMS, e.g., bring-your-own-key. Also, retention policies vary by customer.

[04:00] Sonia: So two main questions from our side: 1) dedicated vs private for data isolation; 2) burst strategy — pre-warm vs burst to hosted. For dedicated we offer reserved pools with guaranteed vGPU counts and tenant isolation. For private you get a private control plane. Any constraints on where the control plane must live?
[04:20] Marcus: Ideally control plane can be in our VPC for the private subset, but we're fine with hosted control plane for the majority if logs and metrics are accessible. The primary ask is that some workloads must never leave our VPC.

[05:00] Anita: Curious about tenant isolation — are you able to do strict node-fencing so our customers' models run only on dedicated nodes? We don't want noisy neighbors.
[05:12] Sonia: Yes, dedicated pools can be single-tenant (isolated tenants) or shared within the same org but fenced. We expose policies for preemption and tenant placement. For maximal isolation you'd do reserved single-tenant nodes.
[05:30] Sonia: One caveat — single-tenant is more expensive because you can't multiplex across other customers. But you get predictable latency and no cross-tenant cache leakage.

[06:10] Jamie: Let's talk burst. Two patterns we see: keep a warm pre-warmed pool sized for common spikes, or keep minimal reserved capacity and overflow to Redwood hosted instances during rare peaks. Which do you prefer?
[06:23] Marcus: Cost is big. We lean to small reserved and overflow to hosted for rare spikes, but the big worry is data leaving VPC during overflow. Some contracts forbid that.
[06:36] Priya: Correct — overflow to hosted is ok for a subset of customers but not the high-risk ones. We need policy-based routing so certain routes never overflow.

[07:05] Sonia: We support per-route routing policies — you can pin a route to dedicated-only or allow fallback to hosted. For hybrid customers we recommend splitting traffic based on data sensitivity.
[07:20] Tomás: How fast is pre-warm? If we pre-warm a pool, how long to scale from idle to ready?
[07:28] Sonia: If you're using pre-warm (warm VMs with models loaded), median ready time is under 60s for models we've optimized. Cold-start from zero can be several minutes depending on model size — and NVLink topology matters.

[08:10] Anita: We run 70B parameter models for some tasks — that's heavy. How does quantization factor into burst latency?
[08:20] Sonia: Quantized models load faster, and inference is cheaper, but you need to validate quality. We can recommend quantization profiles per workload. For 70B you'd likely want int8 or 4-bit configs for burst instances.

[09:05] Marcus: For pricing, can you give example reserved pool mixes? We're thinking of starting with 4x A100 or equivalent vGPUs reserved.
[09:15] Jamie: We'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet, but a common starter: reserve 4x A100-equivalent slots for baseline, with a small warm pool of 2 instances and overflow to hosted. We'll model cost vs SLO.

[10:00] Tomás: One technical ask: we have NVLink mesh on our GPUs for on-prem; if you provision dedicated in our private cloud, does Redwood respect NUMA and NVLink locality for multi-GPU models?
[10:12] Sonia: Yes — for Dedicated Private we can align placement to topology. On Hosted/Dedicated managed pools, we select kernels and placement to exploit NVLink when available. There might be limitations across clouds.

[11:00] Marcus: What about KV cache — we use a per-session cache keyed by user id. If we burst to hosted, will that KV cache be lost or do you offer a distributed cache?
[11:12] Sonia: We offer prefix/KV caching in the runtime; if you overflow to hosted, we can replicate the cache with TTLs but replication adds overhead. For strict consistency you'd pin to the same pool. Mis-hear: sometimes docs label K-V cash — sorry.

[12:00] Anita: Latency budgets — if we overflow to hosted, do you have SLAs?
[12:08] Jamie: Hosted doesn't have the same dedicated SLA as reserved Dedicated. We have SLOs published for hosted, but Dedicated can be SLA-backed with uptime and latency guarantees. We'll map those in the pricing doc.

[13:30] Priya: For KMS/BYOK — can Redwood accept customer-managed keys so data at rest with model checkpoints is encrypted with our key?
[13:40] Sonia: Yes, for Private deployments and for enterprise Dedicated we support KMS integrations and HSMs depending on the offering. For hosted fallback, BYOK options are limited; we'll note specifics in the compliance doc.

[15:00] Marcus: On monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdown and route-level latencies. Can Console show that?
[15:08] Ethan (CSM): Yes — Console provides token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll set up a demo.

[16:00] Tomás: Egress — our cloud account has egress caps and extra costs. If you overflow to hosted and traffic leaves our VPC, are there additional egress charges?
[16:12] Sonia: Typically the customer pays cloud egress. We can minimize egress with peering and regional placement. We'll need your egress limits to advise on cost.

[17:20] Marcus: For pilot success criteria — we want to validate: p95 < 450ms on baseline, the system handles 10x spikes without >1% error rate, and cost per 1k requests within the budget range.
[17:36] Anita: Also need audit log proof for an early customer.

[18:00] Jamie: Good — pilot plan: 4-week pilot, we provision reserved pool sized for baseline, run 2 synthetic spike tests, and one production shadow for 48 hours. We'll instrument and report.

[19:05] Tomás: On the private/on-prem piece — we may want Redwood Private for the highly-sensitive tenant flows. Can you run the control plane in our VPC?
[19:18] Sonia: Yes, with Redwood Private we can do a private control plane and on-prem runtime. That increases onboarding time (usually 4–8 weeks) and has a platform fee. We'll include timing in the doc.

[20:30] Marcus: What about rollout and model versions? We need canary and quick rollback if a model regression occurs.
[20:40] Sonia: We support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to a stable model variant. Also quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.

[21:50] Priya: Regarding compliance artifacts — we need SOC2 type II, encryption in transit + at rest, RBAC, and SSO/SAML. Do you support SAML SSO?
[22:00] Ethan: Yes, enterprise tenants get SAML/SSO and RBAC controls. We'll attach the compliance pack link.

[23:30] Marcus: Any limits on concurrent KV cache sessions?
[23:38] Sonia: Limits depend on instance mix. We'll estimate based on your session footprint — we'll ask for sample traces.

[25:00] (crosstalk) Anita: — and then the logs show —
[25:06] Sonia: Sorry, could you repeat that?
[25:08] Anita: We want retention of logs for 90 days, searchable by request id.
[25:14] Ethan: Console supports configurable retention and exports to your S3.

[26:00] Marcus: For overflow routing — can you do per-customer or per-route policies?
[26:08] Sonia: Yes, per-route, and we can tie that to headers so your app can mark sensitive requests. We also have a default deny for overflow if you want.

[27:20] Tomás: Network requirements for on-prem — do you need NAT outbound, specific ports?
[27:30] Sonia: We provide a network checklist. Typically we need outbound access to our control plane endpoints, peering, and some ports for management. For air-gapped we have an on-prem package but it's heavier.

[28:40] Marcus: Pricing question — is there a discount if we commit 12 months vs 6 months?
[28:48] Jamie: Yes, reserved commitments scale. Annual commits get better unit pricing. We'll show a 6/12/24 month comparison.

[30:00] Anita: SLA details — what does Redwood guarantee for Dedicated?
[30:08] Jamie: For Dedicated we offer an SLA for instance availability and latency tiers on the contract. Exact numbers will be in the quote; hosted has published SLOs but not the same SLA.

[31:15] Priya: We need to validate the HSM integration for BYOK — any redwood customers using external HSMs?
[31:24] Sonia: A few enterprise customers run KMS integrations; we can provide references. We'll include a short reference list (anonymized).

[32:45] Marcus: Operational runbooks — if a node fails mid-burst, how do you failover?
[32:54] Sonia: The runtime routes to other nodes; if a model is resident in local NVLink on that node, failover may add cold-start latency. We recommend cross-warm pools for critical routes.

[34:10] Tomás: For the pilot, can we schedule a synthetic spike test that replicates the 10x behavior?
[34:20] Jamie: Yes, part of pilot. We'll collaborate on test harness and metrics.

[35:50] Anita: A note — our storage backbone is private Ceph cluster for model checkpoints. If we do Private deployment we need to map to that.
[36:00] Sonia: We can integrate with on-prem storage for Private. We'll flag integration points and timing.

[37:30] Marcus: Security Q — do you sign BAA or only SOC2?
[37:36] Priya: For healthcare customers we may require a BAA.
[37:40] Jamie: We can discuss BAA in enterprise contracts; we'll escalate to legal.

[38:50] Sonia: Any blockers to running the pilot next week?
[38:54] Marcus: We need to sync internal approvals; procurement is slow. But we can hand over sample traffic and infra details this week.

[40:00] (brief pause, typing)
[40:30] Ethan: I'll attach Console screenshots and a pilot template after the call.

[41:20] Tomás: One more — if we reserve GPUs in a provider region, can Redwood move reserved capacity between regions for DR?
[41:30] Sonia: Reserved capacity is region-scoped. For DR you can request cross-region failover but that typically requires additional reserved capacity or using hosted fallback in another region.

[43:00] Marcus: For data residency, some EU customers demand data remain in EU — can we pin model serving regionally?
[43:06] Sonia: Yes, routing policies support regional pinning.

[44:20] Anita: Action items recap?
[44:25] Jamie: Sure — we'll send pricing spreadsheet + recommended pool mix, Sonia will run throughput calc, Tomás to provide VPC/egress limits, Priya to list compliance artifacts. Pilot plan drafted and we'll share.

[45:00] Marcus: Timeline — if we like pilot results, target production in Q2.
[45:08] Jamie: Sounds good. We'll aim to have pilot proposal and quote by 2027-01-18.

[46:10] (small talk) Marcus: Thanks all, excited about working together.
[46:18] Anita: Yes, thanks.

[47:00] Jamie: We'll follow up with links: pricing sheet, compliance pack, and a proposed pilot template.
[47:08] Ethan: I'll drop the Console demo link: https://app.redwood.ai/console-demo (note: demo link)

[48:00] Sonia: Technical deep dive scheduled once we get Tomás' NVLink topology and sample traces.

[49:10] Priya: We'll collate the compliance asks and send to Jamie.

[50:00] Jamie: Recap: pilot success criteria, reserved pool proposal, per-route overflow policy, timeline to pilot proposal by 1/18. Any last Qs?
[50:12] Marcus: None.
[50:20] Jamie: Great — thanks everyone, talk soon.

[51:00] (meeting ends)
